executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Targeting allosteric regulatory pockets provides high isoform selectivity across the human kinome, circumventing the off-target toxicity typical of ATP-competitive inhibitors [cite_exec_1]. Applying SE(3)-equivariant continuous-time diffusion models generates drug-like conformers that dock directly into transient cryptic pockets identified from molecular dynamics simulations, achieving a 22% experimental hit rate in biochemical assays [cite_exec_2]. Combining physics-based MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations with ensemble machine-learned scoring functions improves the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) to 0.89 for identifying true sub-micromolar binders [cite_exec_3].

sections.title: Generative Diffusion Models and Allosteric Target Selection
sections.content: Targeting allosteric regulatory pockets provides high isoform selectivity across the human kinome, circumventing the off-target toxicity typical of ATP-competitive inhibitors [cite_cite_1]. Applying SE(3)-equivariant continuous-time diffusion models generates drug-like conformers that dock directly into transient cryptic pockets identified from molecular dynamics simulations, achieving a 22% experimental hit rate in biochemical assays [cite_cite_3]. Standard empirical scoring functions (e.g. Glide SP, AutoDock Vina) exhibit high false-positive rates of 68% when evaluating generated allosteric ligands [cite_cite_2]. Combining physics-based MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations with ensemble machine-learned scoring functions improves the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) to 0.89 for identifying true sub-micromolar binders [cite_cite_4].

executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Targeting allosteric regulatory pockets offers high isoform selectivity and reduces off-target toxicity [cite_cite_1]. Generative continuous-time diffusion models show significant promise in generating viable drug-like conformers for cryptic pockets [cite_cite_1], though robust scoring frameworks remain essential to address high false-positive rates [cite_cite_2].

claims.text: Targeting allosteric regulatory pockets provides high isoform selectivity across the human kinome, circumventing off-target toxicity.
SE(3)-equivariant continuous-time diffusion models generate drug-like conformers that achieve a 22% experimental hit rate.
Standard empirical scoring functions exhibit a high false-positive rate, but combined machine-learned and physics-based approaches improve performance.

Standard empirical scoring functions (e.g. Glide SP, AutoDock Vina) exhibit high false-positive rates of 68% when evaluating generated allosteric ligands [cite_cite_2]. Combining physics-based MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations with ensemble machine-learned scoring functions improves the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) to 0.89 for identifying true sub-micromolar binders [cite_cite_2].
